sentences.text: Australodocus possessed a shorter neck than other sauropods because its vertebrae were shorter than those of its counterparts and possessed a bifurcate neural spine.
This animal reached an estimated length of 25.00 meters, a height of 7.00 meters, and a weight of 12 tons.
Fossils of Australodocus bohetii were recovered in 1909 from the Upper Dinosaur Member of the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania.
The original series of four vertebrae collected in 1909 was reduced to two surviving pieces after the others were destroyed during World War II.
While initially classified as a diplodocid, recent analyses suggest Australodocus may instead belong to the titanosauriform clade.
Studies by John Whitlock and colleagues found Australodocus to be a member of the Titanosauriformes clade, possibly closely related to Brachiosaurus.

Tschopp et al. (2015) recovered Australodocus as a diplodocine diplodocid related to Supersaurus, but noted this placement was untenable due to its shared somphospondylous internal structure with titanosauriforms.
Mannion et al. (2019) classified Australodocus as a non-titanosaur somphospondyl and considered it a potential euhelopodid based on cervical internal structure.
Australodocus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 147 million years ago in the Tithonian stage, in what is now Africa.
The time range for Australodocus is estimated from 149.2 to 143.1 million years ago.

It is debated whether the higher number of macronarian sauropods in Tendaguru compared to diplodocoids in the Morrison Formation is due to environmental differences, such as conifer forests versus open plains.
